Q: Building monorepo with multiple node.js projects with pnpm A:

This already works with pnpm v10.
The easier way is to add every app via cli like:

pnpm link ./apps/web-app2/

Because every such link command modifies two files:
both package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml,
so they must exist.

And the results looks like

package.json:

  "packageManager": "pnpm@10.33.0",
  "dependencies": {
    "api": "link:apps/web-app",
    "cms": "link:apps/web-app2",
    "player": "link:apps/web-app3"
  }
}

and pnpm-workspace.yaml:

modulesDir: 'pnpm-modules'
overrides:
  api: link:apps/web-app
  cms: link:apps/web-app2
  player: link:apps/web-app3

And with such setup it is possible to:


# install (download dependencies) of all subprojects/modules
pnpm i -r

# run all test in every subproject/module in parallel
pnpm run -r --parallel test

# build every subproject/module in parallel
pnpm run -r --parallel build

# NOTE "test" and "build" must be defined in "scripts" section of every `package.json`

P.S. After all hoorays

So finally Node.js ecosystem has something,
that Java Maven/Gradle has been having for over a decade. But of cause it is not only catching up, it is already few steps ahead with feature like minimumReleaseAge,
read https://pnpm.io/supply-chain-security and real life case of LiteLLM hack

The technical details of the incident are at https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-04-02-incident-report-litellm-telnyx-supply-chain-attack/

Q: Apparently my code is AI generated (Except it's not) A:

AI detectors output false positives even on regular text (considering there are plenty of patterns to check/verify there). So I wouldn't believe any AI detector tool for code, if the code is AI generated, I think 80% you can see that with your human eyes.

Also in regular writing you have flexibility to output a specific idea in a lot of different ways. But usually there are much less flexibility in the correct way of doing things via code (don't throw trash at me, I mean structurally everything is identical, like how would you construct creative/novel code using the same 20-30 keywords solving the same exact problem in a more or less readable and performant way?).

TLDR;
So I wouldn't trust AI detectors.

Q: Is strtol(str, &str, 10) legal in C99 due to restrict aliasing? A:

Is strtol(str, &str, 10) legal in C99?

Yes, it is valid C99.

If an implementation of strtol() were to access the string "1234" via **endptr for any reason, then the restrict promise on nptr would be violated

That'a true. But an implementation doesn't need to make such an access.

Does this constitute a restrict violation according to §6.7.3.1 of C99?

No, it does not.

Specifically:

Does restrict on endptr only constrain endptr itself, or does it also constrain *endptr with respect to nptr?

The former. Or, to be more exact, the restrict on endptr doesn't constrain endptr, it constrains accesses through pointers other than endptr, to the object pointed to by endptr.

However, the restrict on nptr constrains accesses to the object nptr points to, through endptr (and thus also through *endptr).

If *endptr and nptr point to the same memory, is that sufficient to produce undefined behaviour, even if endptr and nptr themselves are distinct?

No, that is not sufficient.

Would a hypothetical implementation of strtol() that accesses the string "1234" via **endptr be considered non-conforming to the C99 standard?

Yes it would. But nobody would write such an implementation, since, again, there is no reason to access the string with **endptr.

Q: GoDaddy ACME tool for Windows server A:

Your core problem is that ACME assumes the server requesting the cert is the same one using it, which doesn't always work if the endpoint doesn't have a native client, or can't validate the domain via DNS-01 or HTTP-01.

An alternative is to centralize ACME in one place where you can run a client and handles all the renewals, then need to distribute the cert files to the servers they need to go. Pro's and Con's.

Q: How to query Intersystems Caché for a list of namespaces via SQL? A:

Instead of 
var CS = "Server=XXXXX;User=system;Password=sys;";

This may work

var CS = "Server=XXXXX;User=_system;Password=sys;";

_SYSTEM (with leading underscore !!) is the default System Manager User
not sure if sys or SYS  for password  (in Caché)

And YES you  should use namespace %SYS

You may create an SQL PROCEDURE to serve your needs:

CREATE PROCEDURE %Z.NSPACE() RETURNS VARCHAR
Language ObjectScript
{
 set (%,%r)=""
 for  set %=$o(^|"%SYS"|SYS("CONFIG","CACHE","Namespaces",%)) quit:%=""  set %r=%r_%_";"
 quit %r
}

and it runs like this, assuming you have access to Namespace %SYS
